question: GQ-006
finding: Bifrost stores every request body TWICE. The duplication is universal, not specific to one provider.

per_request_breakdown_mb.note: anthropic path, 2026-08-04. raw_request and responses_input_history are near-identical in size.

evidence.reading: The same conversation, serialised two ways: once as the outgoing request, once as a replayable history.

universality.reading: Every provider shows the same near-1:1 ratio. This is gateway behaviour, not a property of any one client.

consequence: The disable_content_logging flag is worth roughly TWICE what I estimated. I had costed it against raw_request alone; it also eliminates responses_input_history, which is the same size again. Together they are 2.92 of the 2.92 MB written per request.
what_i_did_not_do: Flip the flag. It is gateway-wide and removes Shaan's ability to inspect any request body, mine or otherwise — an observability decision, not a disk chore, and outside what I decide.
